claim: Taking a break from a problem gives a small average gain over continuous work (about d=0.2 to 0.3), with large spread across studies.
agent_test: Same problem set, same total tokens: continuous attempt vs attempt + context reset + second attempt; expect small gain.

claim: Incubation effects are not special to insight; the unconscious-work account is not established, and a large decision-making replication (N=399) found no unconscious thought advantage. (Meta-analysis k=61, g=0.15, trim-and-fill g=0.018; replication N=399 Bayes factor 7.83 for null; both on decision tasks, none on insight.)
agent_test: Do not build a hidden-work step; test only plain resets.

claim: Preparation length moderates incubation: longer prior effort goes with larger break gains for visual and creative problems, not linguistic ones.
agent_test: Fire the reset after k failed attempts vs at once; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Break content matters little for most tasks; a low-demand filler beat rest only on linguistic problems, and a fresh look after impasse worked whatever its length.
agent_test: Compare empty reset, unrelated light task, and no reset.

claim: Gains from incubation are reported mostly on divergent/generation tasks; effect on convergent insight puzzles is smaller (subgroup means 0.22 to 0.29, differences small).
agent_test: Run reset before generation vs before selection on a generation task and on a puzzle task.

claim: Impasse arises from over-narrow constraints and tight chunks; difficulty in matchstick arithmetic follows constraint scope and chunk tightness, and tautology exposure removes only the constraint difficulty.
agent_test: Add an operator list: name assumed constraints, widen scope, split unit; compare with generic retry.

claim: Representational change is not the whole story: equation value cues and progress-monitoring (hill-climbing) also drive solving, and RCT alone does not predict the value effects.
agent_test: Check whether an explicit hill-climb-failure monitor beats a step-count trigger.

claim: Knowing the solution does not ensure re-solving: nine-dot and necklace hints were often restated but not applied.
schema_part: memory (store procedure, not just insight statement)
agent_test: Give the agent a stated rule from a solved twin problem; measure application rate vs paraphrase.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Insight-rated solving in humans uses the same working memory and attention control as analytic solving, and thinking aloud does not hurt.
agent_test: Compare silent vs written-trace scaffolds on insight items at equal tokens.

claim: Acting on external material raises insight solving severalfold and the restart context matters more than the wait.
agent_test: Let the agent run code or build a scratch object vs reason only in text.

claim: The felt Aha is not a reliable sign of correctness; false and induced insights exist and are held with confidence.
agent_test: Calibrate agent confidence after a reframe against an independent check.

claim: Frontier LLMs score far below humans on insight-style riddles (NazoNazo: humans 52.9%, non-reasoning 7.6%, reasoning 17.6% on the 120-item subset); reasoning models help, size does not.
agent_test: Use NazoNazo-type items as the scaffold test set; renewable items avoid saturation.

claim: LLMs often write the correct answer in the thought log and then do not commit (verification failure 5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers, 4 models).
agent_test: Add a ledger of every candidate seen; commit by test; measure recovered answers.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace 'wait/aha' shifts are rare (about 6.3%) and go with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%, N=723,200), so they are not evidence of restructuring.
agent_test: Compare scaffold with forced restructure vs free-running; do not count 'wait' as success.

claim: Externally forced second passes, especially gated on uncertainty, give measurable gains on math (+7.7 to +8.4 pp) but almost none on crosswords or Rush Hour; budget forcing shows a similar gain.
agent_test: Trigger re-look when sample disagreement is high; compare to always-re-look at equal tokens. Source reports two different sample sizes for the math gain.

claim: Directed offline preparation (sleep-time compute) cuts test-time compute about 5x on predictable-context tasks; it is not distraction-based incubation.
agent_test: Precompute facts from the context before the question; test only where context is reused.

claim: Lateral-thinking benchmarks show a large gap to humans and weak consistency under rewrites; 2023-24 models reach 41-63% where humans reach about 92%.
agent_test: Evaluate on semantic and context rewrites, not only originals.

claim: Distractors and red herrings drive LLM failure: removing them lifts GPT-4 from 6 to 471 solved walls, though variants differ in more than red herrings.
schema_part: O (name the obvious grouping, test alternatives)
agent_test: Add an explicit step to list the tempting frame and test alternatives.

claim: Short targeted hints and short restructure prompts beat long ones; question-asking traces modestly raise other lateral benchmarks (0.4 to 5 points).
agent_test: Compare a short trick-type hint with a long one at equal tokens.

claim: For everyday creative tool use, the main LLM error is infeasibility and constraint violation, not fixation; divergent-convergent helps all tested models, self-reflection only the strong one.
agent_test: Add a constraint and inventory re-read; compare with a novelty push.

claim: LLMs reach classic insight answers mostly by deduction rather than reframing, and are near human or above on old verbal sets (possible contamination). Contamination is now measured for one 2026 model on an expert puzzle set (73% vs 25% chance), so old public insight sets cannot be used alone.
agent_test: Test on new items written after the model cutoff.

claim: Chain-of-thought may induce a procedural set (3 steps instead of 1), but evidence is six items per cell.
agent_test: Re-run with more items and humans.

claim: Insight restructuring is computationally hard in general (NP-hard) but tractable under small restrictions on restructuring steps.
agent_test: Cap the number of restructuring moves per attempt and compare.

claim: Ungated self-review lowers accuracy; gains appear only when an outside check or label decides when to revise. So forced reconsideration needs a check-based gate.
agent_test: Compare reconsideration gated by a code or constraint check against an ungated 'review your answer' pass at equal tokens.

claim: At equal tokens, independent fresh samples beat extending one reasoning trace with 'Wait' (math, up to 22 pts at 16K tokens). This is the nearest evidence for a context-reset operator; no insight-item test exists.
agent_test: On insight items: continue vs reset-and-resample vs reset with a short failure note, same total tokens.

claim: Frontier 2026 models still fail on expert insight-style puzzles: thinking models under 30% for most; errors are missing creative connections and misread clues, not recall.
agent_test: Add a connection-forcing step and a clue re-read; measure on fresh items against higher thinking effort.

claim: Old public puzzle sets can be contaminated: Gemini-3.1-Pro identified true items among perturbed copies 73% of the time vs 25% chance, and scored up to 15-18 pts higher on the Russian original than the English translation.
agent_test: Write new items after the model cutoff in two languages; compare with the public set.

claim: A calibrated correctness signal exists inside reasoning models (probe ROC-AUC above 0.7, ECE below 0.1) but verbal self-reports and 'aha' text do not track correctness; the signal is not reachable through an API.
agent_test: Use sample disagreement as an outside proxy and test its calibration against correctness.

claim: Giving more clues up front helps strong models on lateral puzzles but not weak ones (LatEval); no controlled ablation of short vs long hints exists.
agent_test: Ablate hint length and specificity on a lateral set with a fixed solver.
